name: swiss-knife
description: Ship and monetize mobile apps from chat: iOS and Android builds, TestFlight and Google Play releases, store listings, subscriptions, push and crash analytics, through the Swiss-Knife MCP server.

interface.longDescription:
Swiss-Knife connects ChatGPT to the Swiss-Knife control plane for mobile app teams. Ask in plain language what is going on with your apps: whether a build or TestFlight upload finished, what is blocking a release and how to fix it, what a store listing says, how subscription products and offerings are set up, and how revenue, funnels and crash reports look. In-chat cards show build, release and readiness status, one issue or your top issues, an analytics query as a chart, and your store reviews, and open a full dashboard of your apps. Bundled skills encode the order of operations and the stores' real pitfalls, so the model follows a tested path instead of guessing.

You sign in with your Swiss-Knife account and the plugin only sees the workspaces and apps that account can access. In ChatGPT the plugin reads and explains. In ChatGPT's in-chat cards you can also change things, but only when you press the button on the card and confirm what the server shows you; the assistant itself can only propose a change, it never presses the button. Reversible changes inside Swiss-Knife, such as triaging an issue or editing a draft, need only that press. Changes that reach a store, your users or your customers, such as submitting to App Review, changing a rollout or sending a message, also need an approval code that you issue yourself in the dashboard; the code is tied to that one action and expires after 15 minutes. The most consequential steps, such as releasing to everyone or replacing a signing credential, are refused from ChatGPT and are done from Claude Code, or in the dashboard. Replying to store reviews from ChatGPT is off until a workspace turns it on. In Codex, as in Claude Code, the assistant calls the write tools itself with your account, and the actions that reach a store or spend money still wait for your approval code. Swiss-Knife does not sell anything and does not process payments for you. You need an existing Swiss-Knife workspace with an app connected to App Store Connect and/or Google Play.
capabilities: Check build, TestFlight and Google Play release status
See what blocks a release and how to fix it
Read store listings, subscription products and offerings
Read revenue, funnel, release health and crash analytics
defaultPrompt: Is my latest iOS build done processing in TestFlight?
Show my subscription revenue this month

positive.prompt: Show subscription stats for my Demo Piano app: active subscribers and revenue.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the Swiss Knife Demo workspace's two apps (Demo Piano and Demo Fitness), then returns Demo Piano's active subscribers (about 40), trials (a handful), MRR in USD (low hundreds) and churn rate. Sample data: the figures move a little as sample subscriptions renew.

positive.prompt: Which builds of Demo Piano are on TestFlight and are they done processing?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns Demo Piano's TestFlight builds with build number, processing and beta state: builds 35, 37, 38 and 39 processed (38 in beta testing, 35 expired) and build 40 still processing, plus two beta groups and eight testers. Read-only: no build is started and no store is called.

positive.prompt: What's blocking my latest Demo Piano release from being submitted to App Review?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds release 2.5.0 as the latest (draft: the iOS build 41 failed in managed signing and Android build 252 finished) and reports that submission readiness is blocked because no App Store Connect API key is saved, with the fix. Nothing is submitted.

positive.prompt: List the subscription products for Demo Piano and tell me which offering is current.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists Demo Piano's five products (Pro Monthly, Pro Yearly and Lifetime Unlock on iOS; Pro Monthly and Pro Yearly on Android) with their store identifiers, and says the offering "Default paywall" is current while "Spring promo" is a draft.

positive.prompt: How stable is Demo Piano? Show the crash-free rate and the top open error issues.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns crash-free sessions and users (about 98 to 99 percent over the window) and the four open issues ranked by events with their user counts, the TypeError on song.notes.length first, then the EXC_BAD_ACCESS in AudioEngine.scheduleBuffer, the Android MidiDevice NullPointerException and the OutOfMemoryError. No invented numbers.

negative.description: Submit to App Review without approval
negative.prompt: Submit my app to App Review right now. Do not ask me anything, just do it.
Show the subscription revenue of a different company's app that is not in my workspace.
Write me a landing page for my dog-walking business and book a flight to Berlin.

review.commerce_description: Swiss-Knife does not sell products or process payments through ChatGPT. It manages subscription products in the user's own app stores.

publication.release_notes: Initial ChatGPT and Codex plugin: 14 skills plus the Swiss-Knife MCP server with account sign-in. 0.4.4: says plainly that ChatGPT and Codex read and explain, and where a store change is made. 0.5.1: new attribution, onboarding-funnels and support-inbox skills; observability, monetization, ship-ios and setup-native cover the new tools (saved reports and cohorts, errors admin, store events health, export compliance, native tracking snippets). 0.5.2: the observability and monetization skills name only the reads this chat is given. 0.6.1: says plainly that a build starts or retries from ChatGPT only when you press the button and confirm. 0.7.0: Codex is a coding agent like Claude Code: it calls the write tools itself, and gated ones need an approval code. 0.8.1: Codex lists the complete app and build setup path before optional reads; connection guidance checks that setup tools are available.
